The Trump administration has proposed adding additional tariffs on 14 of the U.S.'s major
trading partners, including the EU, China and Japan, over what the administration says

Some lawmakers have been trying to fight President Trump's tariffs in Congress, including Democratic

A federal judge is blocking the Federal Communications Commission from immediately reviewing the
local TV licenses held by ABC and its parent company, Walt Disney.
As NPR's David Fochenflick reports, the judge says the FCC unconstitutionally retaliated
against the network in response to programming, including news coverage, satire and others
that angered President Trump.
ABC sued after the FCC announced that it would immediately review all eight local TV broadcast
licenses held by ABC and Disney.
The agency had previously launched inquiries into Disney's diversity practices and into
the ABC talk show The View.
Trump had repeatedly called for ABC to be punished for its news decisions and for jabs
at him by late night comic Jimmy Kimmel.
U.S. District Court Judge Lauren Ali Khan called the threat existential and said the FCC's
actions served to chill broadcasters' free speech.
She accused FCC chair Brendan Carr of taking, quote, Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders.
Carr did not return NPR's request for comment.
David Fochenflick, NPR News.
Israeli airstrikes have killed two senior Hamas security officials in Gaza.
As NPR's Anas Baba reports, it's the latest Israeli attack targeting officers in Gaza's
interior ministry.
The first strike on Tuesday killed Hamas's internal security chief in Gaza, Brigadier
General Naim Abunahal.
In a second strike this morning targeted the head of the services in North in Gaza, Colonel
Mohammad Abulov.
Israeli Prime Minister commended the assassination of the two men.
The Hamas-run security forces have been targeting rival Palestinian militias that are armed
and backed by Israel, making them a target of Israeli airstrikes.
Israel dropped leaflets over Gaza, showing the two men's faces crossed out in dread,
warning that anyone who attempts to harm its friends on the ground will face an eye for
an eye in response.
Anas Baba, NPR News, Gaza.
This is NPR News.
EU leaders are working to bridge major differences over the bloc's long-term budget, trying to
agree on a major new loan to support Ukraine.
The 2028-34 budget could amount to between 1 and 1.2 percent of the bloc's gross national
income.
European Council President Antonio Acosta says leaders at the two-day meeting in Brussels
have the responsibility to find a balanced budget agreement that will allow the EU to
take on challenges ahead, but complicating things?
Upcoming elections in Spain this weekend and next year in France, Italy and Poland.
Scientists have identified what could be a new way to spot the chance of a woman getting
pregnant.
The findings focus on the male's contribution to fertility.
They were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences this week,
as NPR's Will Stone reports.
The study from researchers at Wayne State University looked at more than 300 men with
seemingly normal sperm and homed in on what's known as mitochondrial DNA.
The genetic material for mitochondria, which produce energy and carry out many functions
in our cells, is passed down through the mother.
But the study's lead author, Richard Pilsner, says they see that men with sperm that have
greater concentrations of this mitochondrial DNA also have a much higher chance of not
being able to get pregnant with their partners.
Those men that have presumably normal semen parameters, this molecular signature, is tracking
with probability of pregnancy.
It's not clear why this is the case, but Pilsner says the goal is to come up with more precise
ways to measure male fertility.
Will Stone, NPR News.
And I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.
